name: Medic
botanicalName: Medicago truncatula / M. littoralis / M. polymorpha
harvestProduct: grazing / dry pods (self-reseeding pasture ley) — not a harvested food crop

evidence.quote: Suited Regions: Western Cape, Southern Cape and Eastern Cape
Suited Regions: Western Cape, Southern Cape and Eastern Cape. Planting Months: Apr - May

Bur Medic (Medicago polymorpha) is a legume that is closely related to alfalfa/ lucerne. They fix around 120kgN/ha. They are true annuals flowering, setting seed and dying within one growing season (60 to 100 days).
evidence.doc: Conservation Agriculture Manual, Chapter 5: Cover crops, Grain SA, 2016

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Whole annual life cycle (germination to seed set/death) for bur medic, not a specific pasture-cut date.

evidence.quote: Seeding: 4-7kg/ha if sown in mixture, 10-12kg/ha planted, 12-15kg/ha broadcast
DM yields of 5mt/ha are obtainable with a carrying capacity of 4-5 small stock units during winter to 10 small units/ha during spring are possible

evidence.doc: Conservation Agriculture Manual, Chapter 5: Cover crops, Grain SA, 2016

evidence.quote: Medics is also an outstanding rotational crop with cereals and the advantages are the fixing of nitrogen, the reduction of diseases and the controlling of weeds

varieties.name: Parabinga, Paraggio, Santiago, Cavalier, Bindaroo
varieties.note: Medicago truncatula, M. littoralis and M. polymorpha cultivars; well drained loam to clay soils; hard seed coat lets the pasture re-establish itself the following year without re-sowing.

evidence.quote: Due to the hard seed coating the seed is able to establish itself the following year again.

zoneNotes.western-cape: Winter-rainfall wheat/pasture rotation crop, sown Apr-May, on well-drained loam to clay soils.
zoneNotes.southern-cape: Included by Agricol among the suited regions for medics, alongside Western and Eastern Cape.
zoneNotes.karoo-arid: Grain SA CA manual notes medics are 'used very successfully in dryland conditions with poor quality soils.'

gaps: No row/in-row spacing found — medics are established as a broadcast/drilled pasture, not a row crop, in the sources found.

daysToHarvestRange (60-100 days) is for the closely related Bur Medic's full annual cycle, used here as the best available proxy for the Medicago truncatula/littoralis/polymorpha group sold by Agricol, since no separate cycle-length figure was found for those species.
summary: Well sourced for winter-rainfall sow window (Apr-May), seed rate (4-15 kg/ha depending on method), DM yield (5 t/ha) and N-fixation (~120 kg/ha) from Agricol's Medics page and the Grain SA CA manual's Bur Medic entry. Row/in-row spacing and sow depth are not given anywhere (medics are broadcast pasture, not row-planted), so the entry stops at 'partial'.
